key_insight: This paper presents a brain-inspired generative model that can sample from cognitive maps to support goal-directed imagination and planning. The key advance is that it achieves these abilities using stochastic computation and compositional coding with only local synaptic plasticity.
problem_solved: AI systems often struggle to flexibly imagine future states, plan toward goals, and solve novel problems without heavy global training signals or handcrafted search procedures. This work addresses how to build a more biologically plausible model that supports planning from internal world representations.
method: Represents knowledge as cognitive maps that can be sampled to generate possible future trajectories.
Uses stochastic computing to enable flexible, goal-directed imagination rather than deterministic prediction only.
Employs compositional coding so complex states and plans can be built from reusable components.
Learns with local synaptic plasticity, avoiding dependence on non-biological global optimization mechanisms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a route toward more efficient, interpretable, and brain-inspired planning systems. It may inspire models that combine generative imagination with local learning rules for tasks like navigation, decision-making, and problem solving.

paper_title: Neural sampling from cognitive maps enables goal-directed imagination and planning
paper_authors: Hui Lin, Yukun Yang, Rong Zhao, Giovanni Pezzulo, Wolfgang Maass
